dialogue:
JAMIE: Today I want an AI agent that knows when to stop talking. A radical concept in this studio.
RUFUS: I assumed your segment had been cancelled.
JAMIE: Lovely. You can be my first difficult customer.
ALEX: He has been preparing for this role his entire life.
JAMIE: Our example is hypothetical: a birthday present says delivered, but the doorstep is empty. The clock is ticking, and a cheerful chatbot keeps asking whether you have checked the doorstep.
RUFUS: Perhaps the present has achieved autonomy.
JAMIE: Exactly the sort of answer that gets you transferred. Salesforce's public Trailhead material describes Agentforce for Service examples covering delivery questions and escalation. This is existing guidance checked today, not a new launch or a customer success claim.
ALEX: So what should our imaginary shop build?
JAMIE: A useful path for an ordinary delivery question, and a clear exit when the parcel is missing or the person asks for human help. Start with those three test requests before letting it near real customers.
RUFUS: And somebody actually has to answer at the other end. An escape hatch into an empty cupboard is not customer service.
JAMIE: Thank you! That is the point. I like automation when it removes effort. I do not like automation that makes the customer prove they deserve a person.
ALEX: Rufus agreeing with Jamie. We should probably preserve this recording.
RUFUS: I shall deny nothing. Especially if she finds my hypothetical present.
JAMIE: In the test environment, check which request routes where, whether a human receives it, and what information arrives with it. That last part is our proposed test, not a claim that every installation already passes.
ALEX: Because nobody wants to explain the missing parcel all over again.
JAMIE: Right. Your first step is to write those three fictional messages. Then have your administrator test the configured workflow. Access depends on your Salesforce setup; private actions need additional configuration. The learning page is not a ready-made deployment.
RUFUS: Nor proof that it saves money.
JAMIE: No measured savings claimed. My verdict: the best agent is not the one that handles absolutely everything. It is the one that helps, recognises its limit, and gets the right person involved.
RUFUS: A modest ambition. We have yet to achieve it in several committees.
ALEX: Including this one?
JAMIE: This one has excellent escalation. I just interrupt you.
